THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 439 OF THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN CR.NO.60/2022 OF HIGH GROUNDS P.S. BENGALURU CITY FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 420,465,468,471,120B READ WITH SECTION 34 OF IPC ON THE FILE OF THE XXIII ADDL.CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND SPL.JUDGE (P.C.
ACT) BENGALURU.
THIS CRIMINAL PETITION HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR ORDERS ON 14.02.2023, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused No.30 under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., for granting regular bail in Crime No.60/2022 registered by High Grounds Police Station, Bengaluru and filed the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 36, 37, 119, 409, 420, 465, 468,
471, 201 read with 34 of IPC and section 7a, (c), 7a and 8, 13 (1) (a) read with 13 (2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
2.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and learned special counsel for the respondent.

3. The case of the prosecution as per the charge sheet against this petitioner is that the accused No.11 said to be a candidate who was aspirant of the PSI who took the PSI examination and he approached the present petitioner accused No.30 - Second Division Assistant, who was working in police department, for doing favour to him by manipulation of the answers and to give more marks in the examination and the accused No.30/present petitioner introduced the accused No.29 who is FDA in the Police Department Recruitment wing.
Accordingly, the accused No.29 in collusion with higher official said to have manipulated the OMR answer sheets.

Even though this petitioner answered 19 questions, subsequently the accused persons manipulated the answer sheet by showing he has answered 99 questions and gave more marks for facilitating him to be selected in the PSI examination.
This petitioner was arrested by the police and was remanded to the judicial custody.
Previously his bail petition was dismissed as withdrawn and now he is before this court with additional grounds.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence,
except introducing the accused No.17 to the accused No.29, he has not done anything and he has also not received any amount from the accused No.11.
The investigation is completed charge sheet has been filed.

All the co-accused persons who are beneficiaries are granted bail by the Sessions Judge but rejected the bail petition of this petitioner who is a public servant, he has been implicated only on the voluntary statement of the co accused hence, prayed for granting bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Special counsel for the respondent seriously objected the petition and contended that previously the case has been registered in Kalaburagi police and thereafter investigation taken by the CID police, there was huge malpractice in the PSI recruitment.
One of the accused was caught red handed by using the device and ear phone and later it was revealed that the OMR sheets were tampered by the accused persons.
The accused Nos.29 to 35 are the Public Servants.
They committed the heinous offence and the FSL report clearly reveals the malpractices done by the accused persons.
The bail petition of the co-accused No.34 has been dismissed by the coordinate bench.

There is material placed on record, to show the amount of Rs.45 lakhs has been paid by the accused No.11 through this petitioner who is accused No.30, therefore, it is contended that the petitioner is not entitled for bail, hence prayed for rejecting the bail petition.

6. Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records and on perusal of the same, it is not in dispute that there was malpractices in the PSI recruitment where the Public Servants being police officials and staffs, in collusion with the middlemen received amount from the candidates and allowed them to secure high marks and one of the accused has been caught red handed while getting answers through ear phone by keeping a device in the shirt collar.

Thereafter, it was revealed that the accused persons, by receiving the money instructed the candidates to answer only few questions either 9 questions or 19 questions but they used to show they attended 99 questions.

Subsequently,
the OMR sheets said to be taken out from the strong room and correct answer to the questions by marking, the accused persons made those persons to secure more marks for getting through the PSI examination.
It is seen from the records, the accused No.11 is relative of this petitioner who approached him for helping in the recruitment.
Therefore, this petitioner is an SDA working in the police Headquarters DIG Office, introduced accused No.30 who is First Division Clerk as well as a member of the recruitment team.
Subsequently, the accused No.30 received Rs.2 lakhs from the accused No.11 through this petitioner who is relative of the accused No.11.
The further records reveals, thereafter Rs.43 lakhs have been paid by the accused No.11, through this petitioner/accused No.30.
Inturn the accused No.30 said to have given the same to the higher officials.

The coordinate bench while dismissing the application bail petition of the accused No.17-PSI had elaborately dealt with the matter and had dismissed the petition, which is held as under:-
"16.

The allegations which are supported by prima-facie materials, including the FSL report, produced along with the charge sheet by the Investigating Officer constitute a heinous socio- economic offence committed by the persons in power and position.
The manner in which the conspiracy was said to have been carried on, discloses that the accused are capable of corrupting any system for their lust for money.
A dacoit may commit the offence to earn some money for his livelihood or even to lead a lavish life.
A murderer may commit the offence to end the life of another person for his own reasons.
Such offences may destroy the lives of such families or few others.

But the allegations made against the accused disclose that the persons who are in high position and power, who are expected to be the role models for any youngster, have stooped to such a level in their crave for money, in spite of enjoying everything in life which a persons may dream of in his life.
The offence alleged is much more serious than committing any heinous murder or dacoity or any other offence for that matter.

As rightly contended by the learned Prosecutor, the act of the accused demolishes the Mr R Manjuanth vs State Of Karnataka on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169930756/
3 edifice of rule of law and destroys the confidence of the general public in the system.

sentences.text: 17. It is stated that about 55 thousand youngsters with the fond hope of getting their dream job toiled day and night in making preparations for facing the examination as aspirants for the post of Sub-Inspector of Police.
There may be few thousands of meritorious candidates who must have burnt the midnight oil to fair well in the examination.
There may be many such candidates who might have attempted the examination as a last attempt to reach their dream job in view of their advanced age.
There may be several such candidates who must have dreamt of bringing a change in the Society and to serve the general public by joining the service in the Department.
There may be many such parents who must have dreamt to see their wards in a responsible position in service of the Society.
The act of the accused destroyed all these aspirations.
It may not be strange if such eligible candidates and their entire family loose faith in the system and hope in their life.
A reasonable impression may be created in the Society as a whole that the entire system is corrupt.
When the Society start admitting that the system itself is corrupt, it will be a very dangerous situation for any civilized Society.
The officers in the Department will have onourous responsibility of investigating in to a crime, maintenance of law and order in the society and also enforcement of social legislations.
They are supposed to be the champions for any peaceful society.
When candidates enter the system with corrupt means, we cannot expect that there will be any system worth mentioning to safeguard the interest of the citizen.
It is rightly said that corruption is like cancer in our Society."

In view of the observation made by the coordinate bench and looking to the case of the accused,
though this accused did not receive any commission, but he is the main cause for meeting the accused No.29 by the candidate and paying the huge amount of Rs.45 lakhs for selection of the accused No.11 in the PSI recruitment.
The coordinate bench also rejected bail petition of other accused on 22.7.2022 .
The alleged offence is serious one and if the petitioner is granted bail, there is every possibility of tampering the witnesses, is not ruled out.
Therefore, I am of the view the petitioner has not made out a case of exercising power of section 439 of Cr.P.C for granting bail.
Accordingly, bail petition filed by accused No.30 is hereby dismissed.
